title: Alex: Android XR in Three Minutes
author: Agile Lens
source: Original text created for the Understudy sample pack, October 28, 2026. Not a quotation or a device-readiness claim.

scenes.location: Demo walkthrough, about three minutes at 130 words per minute

entries.text: Original rehearsal text. Pause and resume at your own pace.

Hi, I’m Alex. I make spatial tools for people who work with performance, film, and real spaces. I want to show you a few things we are testing on Android XR. I’ll keep the working pieces separate from the pieces that still need work.

I’ll start with the XREAL Aura. The first thing to look for is presence: does the character feel like it is sharing this room? If the MetaHuman build is ready, I’ll use that. Watch the head, the hands, and the response when I move.

The next part is AuraColocate. The point is a shared space. Two people should agree about where the character is. If we have a second device ready, I’ll show that agreement directly. If we don’t, I’ll tell you what we have actually tested.

Underneath this work is our Unreal 5.8.4 fork. We have been working on foveation, live controls, and hands. I’m interested in what those changes let us do in a scene, and what the device measurements say. I’ll use the numbers from this build rather than guess.

I also want to show the splat work from the UOXR showcase. A captured place gives us a different starting point from a modeled set. Look at the edges and what happens when I change my viewpoint. If that build is not ready, I’ll skip it and show you the next working piece.

Stage Presence is another way into the same question: how do you feel another person in a space? I’ll show the Aura version if it has passed its device check. I’m not going to turn a build that merely compiles into a claim that it works.

Now for a smaller display. This is the Teleprompter inside Understudy. The phone holds the controls, and the AI glasses show my next words. This is a separate glasses companion demonstration. It is not proof that the Aura runs this projected-display path.

I can pause, look at you, and pick up the thought again. I can use a short prompt or a flowing script. For an actor, teacher, or presenter, that is the test: does the tool help me stay with the person in front of me? Tell me where your attention went.
